sources.title: Contents - Playing to Win
sources.notes: Used to cross-check the eight numbered chapters, introduction, conclusion, and appendixes.

sources.title: One: Strategy Is Choice - Playing to Win
sources.role: authorized preview support for Chapter 1 and Olay turnaround framing
sources.notes: Supports the Olay turnaround as the opening anchor and confirms that strategy is framed as a set of choices rather than a plan or vision.

sources.title: Two: What Is Winning - Playing to Win
sources.role: authorized preview support for Chapter 2 winning aspiration logic
sources.notes: Supports the distinction between mission and winning aspiration and names the play-to-win versus play-to-play contrast.

sources.title: Four: How to Win - Playing to Win
sources.role: authorized preview support for Chapter 4 and the Glad case opening
sources.notes: Supports the ForceFlex / Glad case as the entry point for the how-to-win discussion.

sources.title: Six: Manage What Matters - Playing to Win
sources.role: authorized preview support for Chapter 6 management-systems logic
sources.notes: Supports the chapter's claim that strategy fails without supporting systems, review processes, and measures.

sources.title: Seven: Think Through Strategy - Playing to Win
sources.role: authorized preview support for strategy logic flow framing
sources.notes: Supports the move from the five-question cascade into the practical question of where to start and how to generate possibilities.

sources.title: Eight: Shorten Your Odds - Playing to Win
sources.role: authorized preview support for reverse engineering and uncertainty framing
sources.notes: Supports the chapter's argument that strategy work should shorten odds rather than promise certainty.
